School-level companion table to MathAchieve (per-school demographics incl. MEANSES, Size, Sector, HIMINTY); each School appears once per row, so no grouping factor carries repeated observations, and the help page documents no model. A between-school covariate table, not a grouped dataset.

Weighted ordinal regression clm(income ~ year, weights=pct) on a 2-year by 7-class income distribution (percentages, adopted from McCullagh 1980). year is a 2-level fixed covariate and there is no clustering column; the 14 rows are aggregated percentages, not repeated observations of any group.

Wide format: four repeated ordinal responses y1-y4 (the four visits) as columns plus trt, one row per patient, no within-table cluster column. The example reshapes to long and creates id before the ordgee fit (Miller et al. 1993).

Wide format: four 2-week seizure counts y1-y4 and the baseline count base as columns, one row per subject, no within-table cluster column. The example reshapes to long and creates id before the GEE fit (Thall & Vail 1990).
Subset of spruce: the spruce help-page example constructs sitka89 <- spruce[spruce$wave > 5,] (the second growing season). Same source geepack; the full table spruce is kept.

Uniformity trial of rice, 3 years on the same land; help examples give only desplot heatmaps and yearly means, no model with a random term. total is a mostly-missing alternate yield.
Uniformity trial of rice; help examples give only a desplot heatmap and a Smith plot-size index, no model with a random term; only row/col coordinates and yield.
Uniformity trial of cotton; help example is a single desplot heatmap, no model; only row/col coordinates and yield.

Uniformity trial of bush beans; help computes a raw CV and a desplot heatmap only, no model; only row/col coordinates and yield.

Wide (one row per subject) twin of armd: the visual4/visual12/visual24/visual52 columns are armd's repeated visual-acuity measurements spread across columns. Help page cross-references armd and armd0.

Fiber-level component of prt (same fiber rows, subject covariates dropped); prt is the merged modeling table (prt help: prt was obtained by merging prt.subjects and prt.fiber).
Subject-level twin of prt: one row per the 63 subjects, no within-subject replication; prt is the fiber-level modeling table.
Uniformity trial (Navel 2 at Antelope orange grove): only row, col and yield; examples fit only desplot, no treatment or documented random factor.
Counts aggregated across the 15 blocks (freq is a frequency table); the documented model glm.nb(borers ~ 0+treat) has no random effect and block is not in the table.
Uniformity trial of sugarcane: only row, col and yield; examples fit only desplot, no treatment or documented random factor.
Aggregated contingency table (count per sex x age x score cell); documented model clm(score ~ sex*age, weights=count) is a fixed-effects ordinal model with no random/grouping factor.
Table holds treatment means (each of the 72 factorial treatments averaged over its four reps); no replicate/block column, all factors fixed, examples fit no model.
Documented analysis fits a fixed-effects response-surface lm per crop subset (yield ~ N+P+sqrt terms); rep is a replicate (not block) and enters no model; no random/grouping term documented.

Uniformity trial of oats: only row, col and yield; examples fit only desplot, no treatment or documented random factor.
